statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

\label{lemma-stack-in-setoids-descent}
Let $\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{Z}$ be stacks in groupoids
over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. Suppose that $\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$
and $\mathcal{Z} \to \mathcal{Y}$ are $1$-morphisms.
If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{Y}$, $\mathcal{Z}$ are representable by algebraic spaces
$Y$, $Z$ over $S$,
\item the associated morphism of algebraic spaces $Y \to Z$ is surjective,
flat and locally of finite presentation, and
\item $\mathcal{Y} \times_\mathcal{Z} \mathcal{X}$ is a stack in
setoids,
\end{enumerate}
then $\mathcal{X}$ is a stack in setoids.

\label{lemma-second-diagonal}
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a category fibred in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Delta_\Delta : \mathcal{X} \to
\mathcal{X} \times_{\mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}} \mathcal{X}$
is representable by algebraic spaces,
\item for every $1$-morphism $\mathcal{V} \to \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}$
with $\mathcal{V}$ representable (by a scheme) the fibre product
$\mathcal{Y} =
\mathcal{X} \times_{\Delta, \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}} \mathcal{V}$
has diagonal representable by algebraic spaces.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-check-representable-limit-preserving}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\kappa = \text{size}(T)$ for some $T \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$.
Let $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism
of categories fibred in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{Y} \to (\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is limit preserving on objects,
\item for an affine scheme $V$ locally of finite presentation over $S$ and
$y \in \Ob(\mathcal{Y}_V)$ the fibre product
$(\Sch/V)_{fppf} \times_{y, \mathcal{Y}} \mathcal{X}$ is representable
by an algebraic space of size $\leq \kappa$\footnote{The condition on
size can be dropped by those ignoring set theoretic issues.},
\item $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$ are stacks for the Zariski topology.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f$ is representable by algebraic spaces.

statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is formally smooth on objects if, for every square-zero closed immersion of affine schemes $U\hookrightarrow U'$, an object $y'\in\mathcal Y(U')$, an object $x\in\mathcal X(U)$ and an isomorphism $p(x)\cong y'|_U$, there is an $x'\in\mathcal X(U')$ and isomorphisms $x'|_U\cong x$, $p(x')\cong y'$ compatible with the given one. statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

Fix $d\ge1$. For a morphism $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fppf stacks in groupoids, the relative finite Hilbert stack $\mathcal H_d(\mathcal X/\mathcal Y)$ has over a scheme $U$ objects $(Z\to U,y,x,\alpha)$, where $Z\to U$ is finite locally free of constant rank $d$, $y\in\mathcal Y(U)$, $x\in\mathcal X(Z)$, and $\alpha:y|_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}F(x)$ is an isomorphism. Morphisms consist of compatible base changes and isomorphisms of the displayed data. The absolute $\mathcal H_d(\mathcal X)$ forgets the target $\mathcal Y$, and $\mathcal H_d$ is the finite Hilbert stack of degree-$d$ finite locally free schemes. Natural forgetful maps send $(Z,y,x,\alpha)$ to $y$ and to the underlying $(Z,x)$ respectively.

Consider a $2$-commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{X}' \ar[r]_G \ar[d]_{F'} & \mathcal{X} \ar[d]^F \\
\mathcal{Y}' \ar[r]^H & \mathcal{Y}
}
$$
of stacks in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ with a given
$2$-isomorphism $\gamma : H \circ F' \to F \circ G$. In this situation we
obtain a canonical $1$-morphism
$\mathcal{H}_d(\mathcal{X}'/\mathcal{Y}') \to
\mathcal{H}_d(\mathcal{X}/\mathcal{Y})$.
It commutes with the natural forgetful morphisms to the target stacks and to the absolute finite Hilbert stacks.
